messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Sev2 - Beryl (enterprise VPC) - kv/prefix cache hit-rate collapse detected on dedicated pool dp-3. Auto-pager triggered.
incident-bot: Symptoms: customer API 5xxs up ~18%, p95 latency +1.2s, tenant-level kv evictions spike. Link: https://dashboard.redwood/alerts/2168002468
sara_oncall: acked — I'm oncall. grabbing kv stats now. tagging eng-runtime and tenant ENG. @miguel_runtime @julia_tenant_eng please standby.
miguel_runtime: on it, will pull eviction histogram and recent admission logs. my hypothesis: prefix-noise from a bursty importer causing massive unique key churn + prefetching, polluting shared slab.
sara_oncall: run these quick checks: `kv_cachectl stats --pool dp-3 --tenant beryl` and `kv_cachectl top-prefixes --tenant beryl --limit 25`

# output (from dp-3 node-7)
tenant: beryl
global_hit_rate: 0.03
tenant_hit_rate: 0.02
evictions_per_sec: 15340
active_items: 1.2M
prefetch_queue_len: 820
top_prefixes_unique_count (last 5m): 1.1M

julia_tenant_eng: that's brutal, tenant-level hit rate at 2% — essentially cold. We pushed an integration yesterday that does a lot of ephemeral prefixes for tracing IDs. Customer success (lena_support) is on the phone.
lena_support: on the call with Beryl now — they're seeing a big import job they didn't expect. Asking them to throttle at source. ETA for partial throttle ~10m.
miguel_runtime: suggested quick mitigations to reduce cross-tenant impact: 
1) disable kv prefetch for tenant Beryl (stops background work that amplifies noise)
2) apply admission filter for tenant (reject extremely-low-frequency prefixes)
3) move tenant to isolated slab or dedicate a small slab to avoid hurting other tenants
4) if needed, temporarily route Beryl to a dedicated fallback node group (higher cost, isolates performance)
sara_oncall: execute 1 and 2 now. I'll coordinate with infra to allocate slab after we confirm hit-rate recovery.

sara_oncall: `kv_prefetch_ctl disable --tenant beryl --pool dp-3`
ops-escalation-bot: command accepted; prefetch disabled for tenant beryl on dp-3 nodes [node-5,node-6,node-7].

sara_oncall: `kv_cachectl set-admission --tenant beryl --min-frequency 5 --window 300`
miguel_runtime: admission set. this will block cold, one-off prefixes from entering main cache for 5m window. should cut churn quickly.

nick_dedicated: I'm spinning up two extra dp-3 shards to buy headroom for requests that bypass cache. `poolctl scale dp-3 +2` — estimated time ~90s to add nodes.
nick_dedicated: scale started, nodes coming up. routing will rebalance gradually.

sara_oncall: dumping kv cache eviction logs for analysis: `kv_cachectl evictions --pool dp-3 --since 600s | grep beryl | head -n 20`

```
# sample
[t=2168002560] evict key=beryl:/session/ab34c... reason=admission_reject
[t=2168002561] evict key=beryl:/trace/9f8b... reason=evicted_due_to_churn
[t=2168002562] evict key=beryl:/tmp/uuid-... reason=admitted_then_evicted
```

miguel_runtime: confirms pattern: lots of low-reuse prefixes (session/trace/tmp-uuid). Admission + prefetch disable should dramatically lower evictions. Next, recommend `tenant_isolation` flow to move beryl to dedicated slab with size cap to contain future noise. Need infra approval to create slab id and migrate keys; that is ~15m work.
julia_tenant_eng: we'll coordinate migration but want to avoid full flush that would kill their cache entirely. Suggested plan: create new slab and route new allocations there; aging will naturally move traffic over.
lena_support: Beryl ops says they paused their import for 6m, will keep paused until we confirm improved latencies.

sara_oncall: monitoring p95 and tenant hit-rate now. initial signal: tenant_hit_rate climbed to 18% after admission/pretech changes (10m). p95 improved ~400ms.

incident-bot: Update: Beryl tenant_hit_rate=0.18 (10m post-mitigation), global pool hit_rate=0.69. Error rates trending down.

miguel_runtime: proceed with slab isolation: `kv_cachectl create-slab --pool dp-3 --name beryl-isolate --size-mb 2048` then `kv_cachectl set-tenant-slab --tenant beryl --slab beryl-isolate` (non-disruptive for new keys).

sara_oncall: forging the command now. coordination with infra required for shards that don't support soft partitioning — infra confirmed compatibility.

ops-escalation-bot: slab beryl-isolate created on dp-3 nodes. tenant bound to slab.
miguel_runtime: good. now we should see eviction rate for other tenants drop. monitoring shows `evictions_per_sec` down from 15k -> 1.6k in 8m.

sara_oncall: contacting eng-runtime for post-incident follow-ups: add per-tenant burst protection to runbook, log a new alert threshold on tenant eviction rates and rapid prefix-uniqueness spikes. @miguel_runtime to own postmortem.
miguel_runtime: will own postmortem. immediate next steps: create a regression test that simulates high-entropy prefix flood + prefetch to ensure admission filter + slab isolation handle it.
julia_tenant_eng: coordinating with Beryl to add a client-side fix (reduce ephemeral prefix entropy, reuse stable prefixes) and will verify their import job change later today.
lena_support: customer happy with progress, will keep import throttled for 30m and then ramp slowly.

incident-bot: Severity reduced to P2. Continuously monitoring.
sara_oncall: marking handoff to miguel_runtime for deep-dive and postmortem. I'll remain on standby for any regression for the next 30m.
miguel_runtime: thanks. pulling full perf traces and will schedule a 1hr postmortem. initial root cause: tenant-driven high-entropy prefix stream combined with prefetch + shared slab eviction policy => cross-tenant hit-rate collapse.

ops-escalation-bot: metric snapshot (post-mitigation):
```
pool dp-3:
  global_hit_rate: 0.71
  avg_p95_latency: +120ms vs baseline
tenant beryl:
  tenant_hit_rate: 0.68
  evictions_per_sec: 420
```

sara_oncall: nice recovery signal. I'm going to close the active pager. Please keep updates in this thread if anything regresses.
lena_support: closing the loop with customer; they've confirmed application errors returned to normal. They'll share their import logs for postmortem.
miguel_runtime: will draft postmortem and runbook PR: propose default tenant admission filter, prefetch opt-out config per-tenant, and slab isolation automation for sustained prefix-noise.

sara_oncall: :white_check_mark: incident mitigated. handing to eng-runtime for follow-up.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED - auto-closed by oncall at 2168003322. Follow-up: eng-runtime (miguel), tenant-eng (julia), support (lena) assigned for postmortem and customer remediation.
